newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand decides to stop second airport project.
newsitem.headline: Thailand decides to stop second airport project.

text.p: Thailand's cabinet decided on Tuesday to halt an estimated 100 billion baht ($4 billion) second airport project and concentrate instead on expanding Bangkok's existing Don Muang airport.

Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh told reporters after a cabinet meeting that because the government had to exercise strict monetary discipline, the decision had been made to halt the second airport project.

In December, Italian-Thai Development Plc said it had signed a contract worth 11.65 billion baht ($466 million) to do earthworks for the the second airport project, which was to be built at Nong Ngu Hao on 20,000 rai (3,241 hectres) of land on the eastern outskirts of Bangkok and completed by 2000.

"Due to finance problems, the government forsees that the Nong Ngu Hao project will not be completed on time. So in order to maintain (the) country as a centre for international air transport we had to seek the option to expand the current airport," Chavalit said.

The existing Don Muang airport sits on 800 rai (1,296 hectares) of land belonging to the Royal Thai Air force. The airport can handle a maximum of 31 million passengers and 600,000 tonnes of cargo per year.

The transport and communication ministry would set up a committee to study the plan to expand the existing airport. The cost and details of the expansion would be discussed later, Suvit Liptapallop, the transport minister said.
The nearly four-decades-old Nong Ngu Hao project was initiated in 1960 but due to indecision on the part of successive governments, little progress was made in the project.

Chavalit, who is also defence minister, said the Thai air force had pledged to cooperate with the government and relocate some air force installments in the area to enable expansion of the existing airport.
The Don Muang airport would be expanded to handle service demands for the next 10 years, he added.

But some politicians and a cabinet member said that the abrupt change in the second airport plan would send a negative signal to foreign investors and firms that had already signed up for related projects.
"This will cause damage to the reputation of the country and discourage investors," said Somsak Thesutin, deputy minister of transport and communication.

The government was committed to honour the 18 contracts it had signed with various companies with a total value of 18 billion baht, an amount which included 6.0 billion baht that has already been paid for land acquisition and relocation of people on that land, he said.
"The government resolution is acceptable but what about the contracts that already (have been) committed on the state's behalf," Somsak said.
